question_text: Move to a serverless solution to analyze data in S3 via SQL. Data needs encryption and cross-region replication. Which solution?
answer_text: Create a new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. Use Amazon Athena to query data.
explaination_text: Athena is serverless SQL for S3. CRR handles the replication, and KMS handles the encryption.

question_text: Restrict connectivity to an external provider's VPC to be private and restricted to a target service. Which solution?
answer_text: Ask the provider to create a VPC endpoint for the target service. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.
explaination_text: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs and services without exposing traffic to the internet or requiring VPC peering.

question_text: Migrate on-prem PostgreSQL to Aurora while remaining online and synchronized. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Create an ongoing replication task. D. Convert the database schema by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT).
explaination_text: SCT converts the schema, and AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) with ongoing replication keeps the source and target in sync.

question_text: Ensure account notifications are not missed and limited to account admins in AWS Organizations. Which solution?
answer_text: Configure all AWS accounts to use the same root user email address. Configure AWS account alternate contacts in the AWS Organizations console.
explaination_text: Alternate contacts (Billing, Operations, Security) allow notifications to go to relevant personnel without using the root user email.

question_text: Redesign a RabbitMQ architecture for highest availability and least overhead. What should be done?
answer_text: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Migrate DB to Multi-AZ RDS.
explaination_text: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service that provides high availability and removes manual RabbitMQ management.

question_text: Automatically move S3 files, run Lambda pattern-matching, and send to SageMaker. Which solution has least overhead?
answer_text: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker as destinations.
explaination_text: S3 Event Notifications trigger downstream workflows automatically, providing an event-driven, low-overhead pipeline.

question_text: Optimize cost for EC2 ingestion (sporadic) and Fargate/Lambda API (predictable). Which purchasing options? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer. C. Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
explaination_text: Spot instances are best for interruptible ingestion. Compute Savings Plans apply to Fargate and Lambda, offering discounts for predictable compute.

question_text: Ensure LEAST amount of latency for a global web portal. How should the solutions architect design this?
answer_text: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to serve content from the ALB in the closest Region.
explaination_text: Latency routing directs users to the region with the lowest network latency, improving the user experience globally.

question_text: High available gaming app supports UDP. Needs low latency, nearest edge routing, and static IPs. What should be done?
answer_text: Configure AWS Global Accelerator to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.
explaination_text: Global Accelerator provides static IPs and uses the AWS global network to route UDP traffic with minimal latency.

question_text: Migrate monolithic app to smaller apps managed by different teams. Highly scalable with minimal overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Host the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up an Application Load Balancer with Amazon ECS as the target.
explaination_text: ECS is ideal for microservices architectures, allowing different teams to manage and scale their own service containers.

question_text: Aurora performance spikes during monthly reports. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
answer_text: Migrate the monthly reporting to an Aurora Replica.
explaination_text: Offloading read-heavy reporting queries to a read replica prevents performance degradation on the primary writer instance.

question_text: Scaling a PHP/MySQL app seamlessly and cost-effectively. Which solution?
answer_text: Migrate DB to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Create an AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group with a launch template using Spot Fleet. Attach an ALB.
explaination_text: Aurora handles DB scaling. Spot Fleets and Auto Scaling handle the web tier capacity cost-effectively.

question_text: Minimize EC2 costs for steady overnight and heavy business day usage. Which solution meets these requirements?
answer_text: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity.
explaination_text: RIs cover the steady 'always-on' baseline. Spot instances handle the daytime surge capacity at a high discount.

question_text: Retain 10 TB logs/month for 10 years. Rarely accessed after 1 month. Which storage option is MOST cost-effective?
answer_text: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
explaination_text: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest tier for very long-term storage of data that is rarely accessed.

question_text: Data ingestion fails due to network issues. How to ensure all notifications are eventually processed?
answer_text: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the on-failure destination. Modify the Lambda function to process messages in the queue.
explaination_text: Using SQS as an asynchronous buffer ensures that if a failure occurs, the request is stored and can be retried until successful.

question_text: Process event data in specific order with minimal operational overhead. How should this be accomplished?
answer_text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set up an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the queue.
explaination_text: SQS FIFO guarantees First-In-First-Out ordering and exactly-once processing.

question_text: Act only if CPU > 50% AND read IOPS is high. Reduce false alarms. What should be done?
answer_text: Create Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms where possible.
explaination_text: Composite alarms can trigger only when multiple conditions (CPU and IOPS) are met simultaneously, reducing alarm fatigue.

question_text: Migrate data center to AWS. Compliance: only use ap-northeast-3 and NO internet access. Which solutions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: C. Use AWS Organizations SCPs to prevent VPCs from gaining internet access. Deny all regions except ap-northeast-3. E. Use AWS Config rules to detect internet gateways.
explaination_text: SCPs provide centralized guardrails to enforce region and internet restrictions. AWS Config monitors and alerts on compliance drifts.

question_text: App used only 12 hours daily. Minimize RDS MySQL costs. What should be done?
answer_text: Create AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the DB instance. Create Amazon EventBridge scheduled rules to invoke them.
explaination_text: Stopping the RDS instance during off-hours stops the compute costs, saving 50% in this specific scenario.

question_text: Downloads are infrequent for ringtones older than 90 days. Save money on storage cost-effectively. Which action?
answer_text: Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
explaination_text: S3 Standard-IA has lower storage fees for objects that are larger than 128KB and accessed infrequently.

question_text: Medical trials: few scientists add files, others read-only. No modification/deletion allowed for 1 year. Which solution?
answer_text: Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days.
explaination_text: Compliance mode Object Lock ensures that even root users cannot delete or overwrite the data for the duration of the lock.

question_text: Cache confidential media files stored in S3 for reliable, quick global delivery. Which solution?
answer_text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to connect the S3 buckets to CloudFront edge servers.
explaination_text: CloudFront caches content at global edge locations, ensuring fast delivery regardless of user location.

question_text: Consolidate batch and stream data. Run one-time queries and show KPIs with least overhead. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight for KPIs. C. Create custom Lambda functions to move records to Redshift.
explaination_text: Athena provides serverless SQL for staged data in S3. QuickSight creates the visual dashboards for management.

question_text: Store Aurora data for 5 years, delete after, and keep audit logs indefinitely. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: D. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster. E. Use AWS Backup to take backups and keep for 5 years.
explaination_text: CloudWatch Logs export allows for indefinite storage of audit logs. AWS Backup centralizes retention policies for the data itself.

question_text: Improve performance for both real-time and on-demand video streaming globally. Which service?
answer_text: Amazon CloudFront
explaination_text: CloudFront is the primary AWS service for content delivery, supporting both HLS/DASH streaming and on-demand file caching.

question_text: Block fraudulent botnet requests to an API Gateway/Lambda app. Which steps? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Create a usage plan with an API key. C. Implement an AWS WAF rule to target malicious requests.
explaination_text: WAF can block requests from known bad IPs or patterns. Usage plans ensure only authorized users with keys can access the API.

question_text: Back up 300 MB JSON/month. Must be accessible in milliseconds and kept for 30 days. Most cost-effective?
answer_text: Amazon S3 Standard
explaination_text: For small datasets (300 MB) needing millisecond access for a short duration (30 days), S3 Standard is simple and cheaper than managing an OpenSearch or RDS cluster.

question_text: Migrate Python app that processes JSON and outputs to SQL to AWS with max scalability and min overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Place JSON in S3. Use Lambda function to process documents as they arrive. Store results in Amazon Aurora.
explaination_text: S3 events trigger Lambda for serverless processing. Aurora is a managed relational database that scales well.

question_text: HPC workflows use hundreds of EC2 Spot instances. Need high performance file system integrated with persistent storage. Which combination?
answer_text: Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3
explaination_text: Lustre is designed for HPC and can be linked to an S3 bucket to automatically load data for processing and write results back.

question_text: Move containerized app to AWS with thousands of users and minimal operational overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Store images in Amazon ECR. Use Amazon ECS cluster with Fargate launch type. Use target tracking scaling.
explaination_text: Fargate removes server management. ECS with target tracking ensures the cluster scales to meet user demand.

question_text: Handle messages between apps. 1,000 msgs/hr. Messages may take 2 days to process. Retain failed messages. Which service?
answer_text: Integrate with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure a dead-letter queue.
explaination_text: SQS can store messages for up to 14 days. Dead-letter queues (DLQ) isolate failed messages for troubleshooting without blocking others.

question_text: Design CloudFront + S3 origin for static site. Require traffic inspection by AWS WAF. Which solution?
answer_text: Configure CloudFront and S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI). Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.
explaination_text: WAF must be applied to CloudFront for global traffic filtering. OAI ensures traffic cannot bypass CloudFront and WAF to go straight to S3.

question_text: Daily HTML reports generate millions of global views. Files in S3. Which action should be taken?
answer_text: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.
explaination_text: CloudFront handles high traffic volumes by caching content globally, significantly reducing the load on S3 and improving speed.

question_text: EC2 app processes SQS messages. Volume is unpredictable but must run continually. Most cost-effective solution?
answer_text: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
explaination_text: RIs ensure constant minimum processing capacity. Spot instances handle intermittent surges at low cost.

question_text: Limit access to specific services in all accounts in an organization from a single point. Which solution?
answer_text: Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.
explaination_text: SCPs allow centralized governance over the maximum available permissions for all member accounts.

question_text: Reduce risk of DDoS attacks against a public web app using ALB. What should be done?
answer_text: Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
explaination_text: Shield Advanced provides dedicated protection for ALBs and direct support from the DDoS response team.

question_text: Application on EC2/ALB must be accessed from one specific country only. How to configure?
answer_text: Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.
explaination_text: AWS WAF has a built-in Geo Match condition that can block or allow traffic based on country of origin.

question_text: Tax computation API experiences holiday spikes causing slow response. Design a scalable/elastic solution.
answer_text: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway. API Gateway passes items to AWS Lambda for computations.
explaination_text: API Gateway and Lambda are both serverless and handle massive spikes automatically with zero server management.

question_text: CloudFront submissions contain sensitive info. Need protection throughout the entire stack. Which action?
answer_text: Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.
explaination_text: Field-level encryption ensures that sensitive data is encrypted at the edge and can only be decrypted by specific applications in the backend.

question_text: Millions of users worldwide access the same videos/images in S3. Reduce load on origin cost-effectively. Which solution?
answer_text: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
explaination_text: CloudFront caches the content globally, so the origin (S3) is only accessed once for each object per edge location.

question_text: Front-end web servers in ASG in a single AZ. Modify infrastructure to be highly available without modifying the app. Which architecture?
answer_text: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use three instances across each of two Availability Zones.
explaination_text: Distributing instances across AZs ensures that the application remains available even if one entire data center fails.

question_text: Ecommerce app surge caused high DB connections and timeouts on Aurora. Prevent errors with least app changes.
answer_text: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy for the database. Modify Lambda to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
explaination_text: RDS Proxy handles connection pooling, preventing the 'too many connections' error common when Lambda scales rapidly against a database.

question_text: EC2 in private subnet needs to access DynamoDB. MOST secure way ensuring traffic does not leave AWS network.
answer_text: Use a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
explaination_text: VPC Gateway Endpoints for DynamoDB route traffic privately within the AWS network, bypassing the internet.

question_text: DynamoDB read-intensive application experiencing delays. Improve performance without reconfiguring the app. What should be done?
answer_text: Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
explaination_text: DAX is an API-compatible cache for DynamoDB. You only need to point the application to the DAX endpoint to get microsecond response times.

question_text: Back up EC2 and RDS data in a separate Region with LEAST operational overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Use AWS Backup to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
explaination_text: AWS Backup is a centralized service that natively supports cross-region backup copies for multiple services with a simple policy.

question_text: Securely store DB username/password in SSM Parameter Store for an EC2 app. What should the solutions architect do?
answer_text: Create an IAM policy that allows read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to the KMS key. Assign policy to EC2.
explaination_text: Standard security practice is to grant specific IAM permissions for Parameter Store and the associated KMS key to the EC2 instance profile.

question_text: Communications platform: EC2 behind NLB + API Gateway. Protect against SQL injection and DDoS. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: B. Use AWS Shield Advanced with the NLB. C. Use AWS WAF to protect Amazon API Gateway.
explaination_text: Shield Advanced protects the network tier (NLB). WAF protects the application tier (API Gateway) from web exploits like SQL injection.

question_text: Rewrite legacy EC2 app to microservices on ECS. Recommend communication method between microservices.
answer_text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add code to producers to send to queue and consumers to process.
explaination_text: SQS is the standard for decoupled, asynchronous communication in microservices architectures.

question_text: Migrate MySQL to AWS. Minimize data loss and ensure transactions are stored on at least two nodes. Which solution?
answer_text: Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance with Multi-AZ functionality enabled.
explaination_text: Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication to a standby node, ensuring zero data loss and high availability.

question_text: Dynamic website needs minimal maintenance, high availability, and rapid read/write scaling. Which solution?
answer_text: Host static content in S3. Host dynamic content using API Gateway/Lambda. Use DynamoDB on-demand. Use CloudFront.
explaination_text: This fully serverless stack provides the highest level of scalability and lowest level of maintenance effort.

question_text: Lambda needs to access a database in a private subnet in an on-premises data center via Direct Connect. Which solution?
answer_text: Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.
explaination_text: When a Lambda is attached to a VPC, it can route traffic through the VPC's resources, including Direct Connect virtual interfaces.

question_text: ECS application needs permission to make S3 API calls. How can this be ensured?
answer_text: Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.
explaination_text: ECS Task Roles provide fine-grained permissions to the containers themselves, rather than the underlying EC2 instance.

question_text: Windows app requires shared file system attached to multiple EC2 Windows instances across multiple AZs. What should be done?
answer_text: Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.
explaination_text: FSx for Windows is the native shared storage for Windows, supporting SMB protocols and Multi-AZ deployments.

question_text: Ecommerce app (LB front-end, container app, relational DB) needs HA with little manual intervention. Which solutions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Create an Amazon RDS DB instance in Multi-AZ mode. D. Create an ECS cluster with a Fargate launch type.
explaination_text: RDS Multi-AZ and ECS Fargate are both managed services that handle high availability and scaling automatically.

question_text: Implement a highly available SFTP solution to upload data to S3 data lake with minimal overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Use AWS Transfer Family to configure an SFTP-enabled server with a publicly accessible endpoint. Choose the S3 data lake as the destination.
explaination_text: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that provides SFTP/FTPS/FTP access directly to S3 buckets.

question_text: S3 documents must not be deleted for 5 years. Encrypt at rest and rotate keys annually. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: B. Store in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode. D. Use SSE-KMS with customer managed keys. Configure key rotation.
explaination_text: Object Lock handles the non-deletion policy. KMS handles managed encryption with automated yearly rotation.

question_text: Java/PHP web app needs testing for new features frequently. Need HA and managed solution with minimal overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping for testing.
explaination_text: URL swapping in Elastic Beanstalk enables Blue/Green deployments for safe, frequent testing of new features.

question_text: A company is developing a marketing communications service that targets mobile app users. The company needs to send its users confirmation messages with Short Message Service (SMS). The users must be able to reply to the SMS messages. The company must store the responses for a year for analysis. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
answer_text: Build an Amazon Pinpoint journey. Configure Amazon Pinpoint to send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream for analysis and archiving.
explaination_text: Amazon Pinpoint is the designated service for customer engagement and mobile messaging. Integrating it with Kinesis allows for scalable, real-time data streaming of SMS responses for long-term storage and analysis.

question_text: A company is planning to move its data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted when it is stored in the S3 bucket. Additionally, the encryption key must be automatically rotated every year. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket.
explaination_text: Using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in AWS KMS allows for one-click automatic rotation every year. Setting this as the S3 bucket default ensures all future objects are encrypted automatically without manual intervention.

question_text: As the company expands, customers report that their meeting invitations are taking longer to arrive. The application runs on EC2 and uses SQS. What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?
answer_text: Add an Auto Scaling group for the application that sends meeting invitations. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale based on the depth of the SQS queue.
explaination_text: Scaling based on the number of messages in an SQS queue (backlog) is the standard way to ensure that as the workload increases, more compute resources are added to maintain low processing latency.

question_text: The company wants to make all the data available to various teams so that the teams can perform analytics. The solution must provide the ability to manage fine-grained permissions for the data and must minimize operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: Create a data lake by using AWS Lake Formation. Create an AWS Glue JDBC connection to Amazon RDS. Register the S3 bucket in Lake Formation. Use Lake Formation access controls to limit access.
explaination_text: AWS Lake Formation simplifies the setup of a secure data lake and provides a central location to manage fine-grained access control for data in S3 and RDS, reducing the burden of managing individual IAM policies.

question_text: A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The company decides to host its website on AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to serve as the CloudFront origin. Which solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.
explaination_text: S3 is the most resilient and cost-effective origin for static websites. Using an OAI ensures that users can only access the files through CloudFront, maintaining security.

question_text: The company needs to design an application that captures AWS API calls and sends alerts whenever the Amazon EC2 CreateImage API operation is called. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert.
explaination_text: EventBridge is designed to react to API changes recorded by CloudTrail in real-time. SNS provides the notification mechanism, making this a serverless and low-overhead solution.

question_text: A company needs to move data from an EC2 instance to an S3 bucket. No API calls or data are routed through public internet routes. Only the EC2 instance can have access. Which solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.
explaination_text: Interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) provide a private IP address within the VPC for S3 access. Combined with bucket policies, this ensures all traffic remains on the AWS backbone and is restricted to specific callers.

question_text: The architecture needs to support distributed session data management. The company is willing to make changes to code if needed. What should the solutions architect do?
answer_text: Use Amazon ElastiCache to manage and store session data.
explaination_text: ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) provides an in-memory, high-performance distributed store that allows session state to be shared across multiple web servers in different AZs, preventing session loss during scaling.

question_text: A solutions architect must provide the quickest solution for identifying all of the tagged components across multiple AWS Regions. Which solution meets these requirements?
answer_text: Run a query with the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to report on the resources globally with the application tag.
explaination_text: The Tag Editor is the native tool for searching and managing tags across accounts and regions in a centralized view.

question_text: A company needs to export its database once a day to S3. Pattern for data is variable and changes rapidly. Data must be immediately available for 3 months. Most cost-effective solution not increasing retrieval time?
answer_text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explaination_text: Intelligent-Tiering is perfect for data with unknown or rapidly changing access patterns, providing cost savings without the retrieval delays associated with archive classes.

question_text: Protect Application Load Balancer (ALB) against common application-level attacks with minimal infrastructure and operational staff. What should a solutions architect recommend?
answer_text: Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.
explaination_text: AWS WAF is a managed web application firewall that integrates directly with ALBs to block common exploits like SQL injection and XSS without needing server management.

question_text: Convert .csv files in S3 to Apache Parquet format and store them in a transformed data bucket with LEAST development effort.
answer_text: Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data.
explaination_text: AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL service that automates data discovery and format conversion with minimal manual coding.

question_text: Migrate 700 TB of backup data from on-prem to AWS within 1 month. Retained 7 years. Infrequent requests. LOWEST cost?
answer_text: Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
explaination_text: Snowball is the most cost-effective way to move petabyte-scale data within a month. Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage for long-term data retention.

question_text: Enable encryption for all existing objects and future objects in an S3 bucket with LEAST effort.
answer_text: Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.
explaination_text: Default encryption handles future objects. S3 Batch Operations is the most efficient way to apply actions (like encryption via a copy command) to millions of existing objects simultaneously.

question_text: Disaster recovery solution tolerating 30 mins downtime and potential data loss. Primary infrastructure healthy check not needed. What should be done?
answer_text: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
explaination_text: Active-passive failover using Route 53 health checks ensures traffic is routed to the secondary region if the primary fails. Cross-region Aurora replicas minimize data loss.

question_text: Web server on EC2 in public subnet. Block all traffic currently. Accessible from everywhere on port 443. Which combination of steps? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0. E. Update the network ACL to allow inbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound TCP port 32768-65535.
explaination_text: Security groups control instance traffic, while Network ACLs control subnet traffic. Both must be configured to allow inbound HTTPS and ephemeral outbound responses.

question_text: API volume is highly variable. Processing takes a few seconds asynchronously. Compute service at lowest cost?
answer_text: An AWS Lambda function
explaination_text: Lambda is highly cost-effective for variable workloads because you only pay for the exact execution time, with zero cost when the API is idle.

question_text: Retain application log files for 7 years. Analysis tool must access files concurrently. MOST cost-effective?
answer_text: Amazon S3
explaination_text: Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective solution for large-scale long-term storage that also allows concurrent read access from various tools.

question_text: Grant access to an external vendor tool in another AWS account without sharing IAM access. How should a solutions architect grant this access?
answer_text: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role.
explaination_text: IAM Role assumption is the standard method for cross-account access, ensuring no static credentials or users need to be shared between accounts.

question_text: Java pod on EKS in private subnets needs to write to DynamoDB without internet exposure. Which combination of steps? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod. D. Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
explaination_text: IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) provide fine-grained permissions to pods. A Gateway VPC endpoint keeps DynamoDB traffic private within the VPC.

question_text: Migrate user activity data capability to AWS. Grow to petabytes. Ingestion facilitating on-demand analytics with SQL. LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
explaination_text: Firehose is a fully managed buffer/delivery service. Delivering directly to Redshift enables powerful SQL-based analytics on the data lake.

question_text: Highly scalable solution minimizing operational overhead for transforms and storing data from millions of remote devices. Which combination? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3. E. Use Amazon API Gateway to send data to Kinesis. Use Firehose to deliver to S3.
explaination_text: API Gateway + Kinesis + Firehose provides a scalable, managed ingestion path. AWS Glue handles the transformation of large datasets in S3.

question_text: Delete objects older than 3 years in MOST cost-effective manner with versioning enabled.
answer_text: Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
explaination_text: When versioning is on, just deleting the 'current' version creates a delete marker. To save costs, the lifecycle policy must be explicitly told to clean up previous (non-current) versions.

question_text: Database not capable of processing volume of write traffic from API. Fluctuating traffic. Ensure data not lost. Which solution?
answer_text: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
explaination_text: SQS provides a buffer to absorb spikes in write requests. Lambda then processes messages at a controlled rate to match the database's capacity.

question_text: Simplify adding/removing compute capacity for MySQL database. Improved performance, scaling, durability with minimal effort. Which solution meets these requirements?
answer_text: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
explaination_text: Aurora Serverless provides automated scaling for both compute and storage without manual management, which is ideal for workloads with fluctuating demand.

question_text: Replace two NAT instances with highly available, fault tolerant, and automatically scalable solution.
answer_text: Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in different Availability Zones.
explaination_text: NAT Gateway is a managed service that scales automatically and offers higher availability than manually managed NAT instances.

question_text: EC2 in VPC A needs access to database in VPC B MOST securely. Both in same account.
answer_text: Configure a VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B.
explaination_text: VPC Peering allows for private, internal communication between VPCs without data traversing the public internet.

question_text: Operations team notified when RDP or SSH access to an EC2 has been established. Which solution?
answer_text: Publish VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create required metric filters. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm with a notification action.
explaination_text: VPC Flow Logs track individual connections. Metric filters on those logs can detect traffic on specific ports (3389 or 22) and trigger an SNS alert via CloudWatch Alarms.

question_text: Secure AWS account root user access. Which combination of actions will accomplish this? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Ensure the root user uses a strong password. B. Enable multi-factor authentication for the root user.
explaination_text: Securing the root account requires a strong password and MFA as the first line of defense against compromise.

question_text: Web-based CRM: EC2 + EBS behind ALB + Aurora. Encrypted at rest and in transit. Which solution?
answer_text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB for transit encryption.
explaination_text: KMS is the standard for at-rest encryption of AWS storage. ACM handles SSL/TLS certificates for encryption of traffic to the ALB.

question_text: Scalable and highly available three-tier application with least amount of change. Which solution?
answer_text: Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments. Move the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve images.
explaination_text: Elastic Beanstalk automates deployment and scaling. RDS Multi-AZ ensures database durability. S3 provides a highly available content store.

question_text: EC2 in VPC-A needs to access files in EC2 in VPC-B. Separate accounts. No single point of failure or bandwidth concerns. Which solution?
answer_text: Set up a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.
explaination_text: VPC peering is highly scalable and establishes a direct network path between VPCs, even across accounts.

question_text: Notified as soon as EC2 instance usage exceeds threshold for individual AWS accounts MOST cost-effectively.
answer_text: Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification.
explaination_text: AWS Budgets is specifically designed for cost alerting and is the most granular and cost-effective method for this requirement.

question_text: Microservice behind HTTPS endpoint using Lambda. Use IAM to authenticate calls. MOST operationally efficient?
answer_text: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.
explaination_text: API Gateway provides a managed HTTPS frontend that natively supports IAM authentication for secure, restricted access.

question_text: Data warehouse solution with Direct Connect. LOWEST data transfer egress cost?
answer_text: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.
explaination_text: Keeping data transfer within the same Region minimizes egress fees, and Direct Connect offers lower egress rates than the public internet.

question_text: PostgreSQL database available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times with LEAST operational overhead.
answer_text: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.
explaination_text: Cross-Region Read Replicas provide data redundancy and disaster recovery capabilities with very little configuration effort.

question_text: IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances returned in response to DNS queries. Which policy?
answer_text: Multivalue routing policy
explaination_text: Multivalue routing allows Route 53 to return multiple health-checked IP addresses for a single domain name, aiding in load balancing and availability.

question_text: Make S3 data available with minimum latency to clinics across country for on-prem file-based apps. What should be recommended?
answer_text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
explaination_text: S3 File Gateway allows on-premises applications to use standard file protocols (NFS/SMB) to access S3 data while caching files locally for low latency.

question_text: Content management system on single EC2. Make website platform highly available and scale. What should be done?
answer_text: Move the database to Amazon Aurora with a read replica in another Availability Zone. Use an Application Load Balancer with an Auto Scaling group across two AZs.
explaination_text: This setup eliminates single points of failure at both the compute and database layers and supports horizontal scaling.

question_text: Configure development environment MOST cost-effectively (ALB + EC2).
answer_text: Reconfigure the target group in the development environment to have only one EC2 instance as a target.
explaination_text: In dev environments, redundancy is less critical. Using a single instance reduces costs while maintaining basic application functionality.

question_text: Web application on EC2 in private subnets. ALB target group EC2 instances. Internet traffic not reaching. How to reconfigure?
answer_text: Create public subnets in each Availability Zone. Associate the public subnets with the ALB. Update the route tables.
explaination_text: An internet-facing ALB must reside in public subnets to receive external traffic, even if its targets (EC2 instances) are in private subnets.

question_text: Submitted data not being processed. CPU utilization at 100%. Improve performance and scale based on load. What should be done?
answer_text: Route incoming requests to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling group based on queue size.
explaination_text: Decoupling the frontend from the processing with SQS prevents requests from being dropped, and scaling based on queue depth ensures capacity meets the backlog.

question_text: Shared storage solution for media app. SMB clients. Fully managed. Which solution?
answer_text: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach it to the server. Connect application server.
explaination_text: FSx for Windows is the primary managed SMB file storage service in AWS.

question_text: Network traffic captured in VPC Flow Logs. Frequently accessed for 90 days, then intermittently. Which configuration?
answer_text: Use Amazon S3 as the target. Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the logs to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
explaination_text: S3 Standard-IA is cost-effective for data accessed once a month or less, matching the 'intermittent access' requirement after 90 days.

question_text: EC2 in private subnet needs to download monthly security updates. No outbound internet currently. What should be done?
answer_text: Create a NAT gateway, and place it in a public subnet. Configure the private subnet route table to use the NAT gateway.
explaination_text: NAT Gateway provides a secure way for private instances to access the internet for updates without allowing incoming public connections.

question_text: Store client case files. Core assets. Growing number. Simultaneously accessible from multiple EC2 instances. Built-in redundancy. Which solution?
answer_text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
explaination_text: EFS is a scalable, redundant file system designed for concurrent access from multiple instances, perfectly fitting the 'core assets' and 'shared access' requirements.

question_text: Policy question.
answer_text: Deleting Amazon EC2 instances.

question_text: Correct issue where least privilege is not applied to EC2 security groups between tiers. What should be done?
answer_text: Create security group rules using the security group ID as the source or destination.
explaination_text: Referencing security group IDs (instead of IP ranges) allows tiers to scale dynamically while ensuring only authorized traffic can pass between them.

question_text: Ecommerce checkout workflow. Users experience timeouts, resubmitting form creates multiple unique orders for same transaction. Refactor to prevent this.
answer_text: Store the order in the database. Send a message with order number to SQS FIFO queue. Set payment service to retrieve and process. Delete message.
explaination_text: SQS FIFO queues ensure idempotent processing, meaning the same order won't be processed twice even if the request is resubmitted.

question_text: Prevent accidental deletion of documents in S3 and ensure all versions available. Combination of actions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: B. Enable versioning on the bucket. D. Enable MFA Delete on the bucket.
explaination_text: Versioning preserves historical states of files, and MFA Delete requires physical hardware authentication to permanently remove any versions.

question_text: Hundreds of .csv files to S3 every hour. Convert to Parquet and place in S3. LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Create an AWS Glue ETL job to convert files. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the ETL job.
explaination_text: Glue is the managed service for format conversion. Triggering it via S3 Event Notifications/Lambda automates the process with no server management.

question_text: Data retention policies for RDS. Retain daily backups for 2 years. Consistent and restorable. Recommendation?
answer_text: Create a backup vault in AWS Backup to retain RDS backups. Create a new backup plan with a daily schedule and 2-year expiration.
explaination_text: AWS Backup is a centralized service that automates retention and lifecycle management for RDS beyond the default 35-day limit.

question_text: Compliance team moving file shares to AWS. Windows Server SMB. Active Directory controls access. Ensure AD groups restrict access to FSx. Which solution?
answer_text: Join the file system to the Active Directory to restrict access.
explaination_text: FSx for Windows File Server integrates natively with Active Directory, allowing current AD users and groups to maintain their permissions.

question_text: Provide customers different versions of content based on devices used. Combination of actions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Configure Amazon CloudFront to cache multiple versions of content. C. Configure a Lambda@Edge function to send specific objects based on User-Agent header.
explaination_text: Lambda@Edge allows for logic at the edge to inspect the User-Agent (device info), and CloudFront caches the resulting device-specific content.

question_text: Provide App VPC EC2s with access to ElastiCache in Cache VPC. MOST cost-effectively?
answer_text: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add route table entries. Configure inbound rule for ElastiCache security group.
explaination_text: VPC Peering within the same region is the simplest and most cost-effective way to connect resources across VPCs.

question_text: Microservices in containers. Minimize maintenance and scaling effort. Cannot manage additional infrastructure. Combination of actions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. D. Deploy an ECS service with a Fargate launch type.
explaination_text: ECS Fargate is a serverless container engine, removing the need for the company to manage underlying EC2 infrastructure or clusters.

question_text: Overcome timeout errors caused by DNS returning unhealthy EC2 instance IPs. Implement what?
answer_text: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a health check in front of the EC2 instances. Route to the ALB from Route 53.
explaination_text: ALB health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy instances. Route 53 points to the ALB, which then handles instance-level failover transparently.

question_text: Highly available application. Web, app, database tiers. HTTPS content delivery close to edge, least delivery time. MOST secure?
answer_text: Configure a public ALB with redundant EC2 in private subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using public ALB as origin.
explaination_text: CloudFront delivers content from edge locations for speed. Using private subnets for instances increases security by isolating them from the direct internet.

question_text: Gaming platform sensitive to latency. Mechanism to monitor health and redirect traffic to healthy endpoints globally. Which solution?
answer_text: Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Add a listener. Add the ALB as the endpoint.
explaination_text: Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to route traffic to the closest healthy ALB, minimizing internet-based latency.

question_text: Analyze data usage in near-real time. Centralized storage in Parquet format. LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze data.
explaination_text: Firehose handles the streaming ingestion and automatic Parquet conversion. Kinesis Data Analytics enables real-time SQL analysis on the stream.

question_text: Improve user experience while minimizing changes to app architecture (MySQL RDS). Which solution?
answer_text: Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
explaination_text: RDS Proxy improves application resilience and scaling by pooling database connections, reducing the load caused by frequent connection opening/closing.

question_text: Increase in read-only SQL queries from business analysts causing performance degradation. Minimal changes. Recommendation?
answer_text: Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
explaination_text: Read replicas are the primary way to offload analytical or read-heavy traffic from the production writer instance.

question_text: Log data in S3. Encrypted at rest before upload. Encrypted in transit. Which solution?
answer_text: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
explaination_text: Client-side encryption ensures data is encrypted locally (on the client) before it even leaves the system, satisfying the 'at rest before upload' requirement.

question_text: Nightly batch job starts at 1 AM. Scale up quickly and down after completion cost-effectively. What should be done?
answer_text: Configure scheduled scaling to scale up to the desired compute level.
explaination_text: Scheduled scaling is the most precise and cost-effective way to handle predictable, time-based workload changes.

question_text: Dynamic website (EC2/ALB) needs to serve multiple languages globally. No recreation across multiple Regions. What should be done?
answer_text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Set cache settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
explaination_text: CloudFront reduces global latency via edge locations, and caching based on the language header ensures users get content in their own language.

question_text: Disaster recovery (DR) strategy with least possible latency. Scale up if necessary. LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?
answer_text: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
explaination_text: Aurora Global Database allows for sub-second data replication across regions and very fast failover, providing the lowest possible RTO.

question_text: DR solution RTO less than 4 hours. Fewest possible resources during normal operations. MOST operationally efficient?
answer_text: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up EC2 instances. Copy AMIs to secondary Region. Automate infrastructure deployment via AWS CloudFormation.
explaination_text: This 'Backup and Restore' approach uses zero compute resources in the DR region until a disaster actually happens, minimizing costs.

question_text: App slow when day begins. Scales overnight to 2 instances. How to address complaints and keep costs to minimum?
answer_text: Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
explaination_text: Scaling out at a lower threshold ensures new instances are ready before the load hits peak levels, reducing the sluggishness felt by morning users.

question_text: Increase traffic causing EC2 overload and RDS out of storage. Predictable but steady growth. Ensure automatic scaling? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS instance. D. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric.
explaination_text: RDS Storage Auto Scaling prevents storage exhaustion, while EC2 scaling based on CPU ensures compute capacity matches traffic volume.

question_text: Transcoding videos. Multiple EC2 access videos for processing. EFS costs too expensive. MOST cost-effective storage?
answer_text: Use Amazon S3 for storing video content. Move files temporarily to Amazon EBS for processing.
explaination_text: S3 is significantly cheaper than EFS for large-scale storage. EBS provides the high performance needed for the actual transcoding work.

question_text: Store employee data in hierarchical relationship. Min-latency response. Monthly email if financial info present. Combination of steps? (Choose two.)
answer_text: B. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store employee data. Export to S3 every month. E. Configure Amazon Macie. Integrate with EventBridge.
explaination_text: DynamoDB offers sub-millisecond responses. Amazon Macie is the standard service for automatically scanning data to detect sensitive financial information.

question_text: DynamoDB backups every month, available for 6 months, retained 7 years. Which solution?
answer_text: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up DynamoDB on first day of month. Transition to cold storage after 6 months. Retention 7 years.
explaination_text: AWS Backup supports lifecycle management, allowing for moving data to lower-cost cold storage and managing multi-year retention policies.

question_text: Advanced analysis on CloudFront logs in S3. Build visualizations. What should be done?
answer_text: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the logs. Visualize results with Amazon QuickSight.
explaination_text: Athena provides SQL access to raw logs in S3, and QuickSight provides the visualization/dashboard layer.

question_text: Compliance standard requires recovery point objective (RPO) less than 1 second. Which solution?
answer_text: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
explaination_text: Multi-AZ RDS uses synchronous replication. Since the data is written to both instances simultaneously before the write is confirmed, the RPO is effectively zero.

question_text: Restrict inbound traffic from ALB to EC2 while preventing other access. Which solution?
answer_text: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
explaination_text: Security Group Chaining ensures that instances only accept traffic originating from the load balancer, which is a key security best practice.

question_text: Report of AWS billed items listed by user for department budgets. Most efficient way?
answer_text: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
explaination_text: Cost Explorer allows for grouping and filtering costs by various dimensions, including tags (like 'user'), and exporting them as CSV files.

question_text: Contact form with dynamic components for S3 static site. Fewer than 100 site visits each month. MOST cost-effectively?
answer_text: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
explaination_text: This serverless approach is extremely low-cost for low-traffic applications, as you only pay for the few seconds of compute used during form submission.

question_text: Website does not reflect updates made in Git. CI/CD verifies successful deployment to S3. What should be done?
answer_text: Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
explaination_text: CloudFront caches objects at edge locations. If the origin (S3) is updated, users will still see old content until the cache expires or is manually invalidated.

question_text: Migrate Windows-based application to AWS. Use SQL Server native backups and share files between tiers. Design architect?
answer_text: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between tiers.
explaination_text: Hosting SQL on EC2 allows full control for native features. FSx provides the SMB file sharing that Windows applications expect.

question_text: Linux web server group needs access to shared file store. No changes to app. What should be done?
answer_text: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
explaination_text: EFS is a managed NFS mount that multiple Linux servers can share without requiring any code modifications to the application.

question_text: Lambda function needs read access to S3 in same account. MOST secure manner?
answer_text: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
explaination_text: IAM roles provide temporary security credentials, adhering to the principle of least privilege.

question_text: EC2 Auto Scaling response to user demand. Optimize cost savings without long-term commitment. Recommend which option?
answer_text: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
explaination_text: Using Spot Instances for the scalable portion of a fleet offers huge savings without the contractual commitment of Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

question_text: Secure video content in S3 via CloudFront. Custom client does not support cookies. Users cannot change hardcoded URLs. Which methods? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Signed cookies. B. Signed URLs.
explaination_text: Signed URLs and Signed Cookies are the two ways CloudFront controls access to private content. If cookies aren't supported, URLs are used; if URLs can't change, cookies are used.

question_text: Ingest real-time streaming data, transform, write to S3, query with SQL. Which solutions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Kinesis Data Streams -> Analytics -> Firehose -> S3 -> Athena. B. MSK -> Glue -> S3 -> Athena.
explaination_text: Both options utilize a streaming ingest point, a transformation tool (Kinesis Analytics or Glue), and Athena for serverless SQL querying on the final S3 data.

question_text: On-prem volume backup to end of life. AWS new backup solution. Maintain local access. Securely transfer. Which solution?
answer_text: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway.
explaination_text: A Stored Volume Gateway keeps a full copy of the data on-premises for low-latency access while asynchronously backing it up to AWS.

question_text: EC2 access S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse internet. How to configure?
answer_text: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
explaination_text: Gateway endpoints provide direct, private routing to S3 within the AWS network, ensuring no traffic goes over the public internet.

question_text: Customer data with PII. Remove PII for two apps, leave for one. LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Store data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning to app.
explaination_text: S3 Object Lambda allows you to run custom code during a standard 'Get' request, meaning you can strip PII dynamically without storing multiple copies of the data.

question_text: Development VPC 192.168.0.0/24. New VPC CIDR block must be valid for peering. SMALLEST block that meets?
explaination_text: VPC peering requires non-overlapping CIDR blocks. 10.0.1.0/24 is a small, valid block that does not overlap with the 192.168.0.0 range.

question_text: Automate scalability. Optimize cost. Enough CPU for surges. Which solution?
answer_text: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Set a target tracking scaling policy based on ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric at 50%.
explaination_text: Target tracking scaling is the most effective way to maintain a steady performance level (50% CPU) by automatically adding or removing instances as needed.

question_text: Process 8 TB. Sub-millisecond latencies. 6 GBps throughput storage. Hundreds of EC2 distribute and process data. Performance requirements?
answer_text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system using persistent SSD storage.
explaination_text: FSx for Lustre is optimized for compute-heavy workloads and provides the necessary high throughput and sub-millisecond latency for parallel processing.

question_text: Migrate legacy app. 24/7 runtime. Database storage growth over time. MOST cost-effectively?
answer_text: Migrate application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
explaination_text: For 24/7 stable workloads, Reserved Instances offer the highest discounts compared to On-Demand pricing for both compute and database layers.

question_text: A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer but needs to control the amount of bandwidth used to minimize the impact on other departments. Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: AWS DataSync
explaination_text: AWS DataSync is a managed data transfer service that simplifies, automates, and accelerates moving data between on-premises storage and AWS. It includes built-in bandwidth throttling controls, making it ideal for migrating 30 TB over a shared network link.

question_text: A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips. Currently, the app uploads raw video clips into an Amazon S3 bucket. Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements to maximize performance and scalability while minimizing operational overhead? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching. C. Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
explaination_text: Elastic Transcoder converts raw videos into formats optimized for mobile streaming (reducing file size), and CloudFront caches this content at edge locations to reduce latency and buffering for global users.

question_text: A company is launching a new application on Amazon ECS using the Fargate launch type. The company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases. What should a solutions architect recommend?
answer_text: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
explaination_text: Target tracking scaling policies for ECS Fargate automatically adjust the number of tasks to maintain a specific metric (like CPU or Memory utilization), ensuring you only pay for the capacity you need.

question_text: A company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in two different AWS Regions on a periodic basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Use AWS DataSync.
explaination_text: DataSync is specifically designed for high-performance data transfers between storage systems (including NFS-to-NFS across Regions) and requires minimal setup compared to manual scripts or third-party tools.

question_text: A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which AWS solution meets these requirements?
answer_text: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
explaination_text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the primary fully managed AWS service that supports the SMB protocol, making it the correct choice for Windows-based shared storage.

question_text: A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges. Which solution meets these requirements?
answer_text: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
explaination_text: A 'cluster' placement group provides low-latency, high-throughput network performance between instances. Keeping them in the same AZ eliminates regional data transfer costs.

question_text: A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its iSCSI storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
answer_text: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes.
explaination_text: Volume Gateway in 'cached' mode stores the full dataset in S3 while maintaining a local cache of recently accessed data, which minimizes on-premises hardware requirements.

question_text: A solutions architect needs to identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed with the LEAST operational overhead. Which solution will accomplish this goal?
answer_text: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
explaination_text: S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility into object storage usage and activity trends, making it easy to spot inactive or underutilized buckets from a single dashboard.

question_text: A company sells large AI/ML datasets stored in an S3 bucket. Customers are in North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce data transfer costs and maintain or improve performance. What should a solutions architect do?
answer_text: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.
explaination_text: CloudFront reduces data transfer costs (as egress from S3 to CloudFront is free) and improves performance via edge caching. Signed URLs ensure that only paying customers can access the data.

question_text: A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances with multiple EBS volumes. The configuration and data need to be backed up nightly and be recoverable in a different AWS Region. Which solution is MOST operationally efficient?
answer_text: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
explaination_text: AWS Backup is a centralized service that automates backups and natively supports cross-region backup copies, providing the most streamlined management.

question_text: A company is building a platform so that authorized users can watch content on their mobile devices. The platform must scale to millions of users. What should a solutions architect recommend?
answer_text: Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
explaination_text: CloudFront scales to handle millions of requests globally. Signed URLs provide a secure mechanism to ensure only authorized users can access the media content.

question_text: A company has an on-premises MySQL database with infrequent access patterns. The company wants to migrate to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of future growth. Which service should be recommended?
answer_text: Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
explaination_text: Aurora Serverless automatically starts up, shuts down, and scales capacity based on application demand, making it ideal for infrequent or unpredictable workloads.

question_text: A company uses an EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an SQS queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining scalability. What should a solutions architect recommend?
answer_text: Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
explaination_text: Lambda is serverless and scales automatically based on queue depth. You only pay when the function is actually running, making it more cost-effective than a running EC2 instance.

question_text: A company needs to implement a solution so that a COTS application (which requires Redshift or S3 data) can use data produced as CSV files in S3 by a legacy application. Which solution has the LEAST operational overhead?
answer_text: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
explaination_text: AWS Glue is a managed ETL service that can easily transform CSV data and load it into Redshift, fulfilling the COTS application's requirements with minimal manual effort.

question_text: A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud and needs a strategy to track and audit inventory and configuration changes (oversized instances, security group modifications). Which actions should be taken? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing. D. Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
explaination_text: CloudTrail records who did what (API calls), and AWS Config tracks the state of resource configurations and alerts on non-compliance (like oversized instances).

question_text: A company must design a solution that provides secure access to hundreds of EC2 Linux instances without using shared SSH keys. Which solution meets this with the LEAST administrative overhead?
answer_text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
explaination_text: Session Manager provides secure remote management through the AWS Console or CLI using IAM policies, removing the need to manage SSH keys or bastion hosts.

question_text: A company needs near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss for JSON data ingested from on-premises sources. Which solution provides this?
answer_text: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
explaination_text: Kinesis Data Streams is highly durable and scalable for ingestion. Kinesis Data Analytics allows for querying the streaming data using standard SQL in near-real-time.

question_text: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?
answer_text: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.
explaination_text: Enforcing a bucket policy that denies uploads without the appropriate encryption headers is the most direct way to ensure all data at rest is encrypted.

question_text: Users upload images to an application. Thumbnail generation takes up to 60 seconds, but the user needs a fast receipt confirmation. How should the solutions architect design the application tiers to be asynchronous?
answer_text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.
explaination_text: Using SQS decouples the receipt of the image from the heavy processing work (thumbnail generation), allowing the frontend to respond immediately to the user.

question_text: Badge readers scan and send HTTPS messages. The solution must be highly available and available for the security team to analyze. Which system architecture is recommended?
answer_text: Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
explaination_text: This serverless architecture (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) is inherently highly available and scales automatically to handle incoming sensor traffic.

question_text: A company wants a DR plan for on-premises file storage (Hundreds of TBs). Users must retain immediate access with no latency and LEAST amount of change. Which solution meets this?
answer_text: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Mount the volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI. Configure scheduled snapshots. Restore snapshots to EBS for disaster recovery.
explaination_text: Volume Gateway 'cached' mode provides local iSCSI access for low latency while continuously backing up the full volume to S3 via EBS snapshots for disaster recovery.

question_text: Application users via Amazon Cognito are unable to access protected protected content in an S3 bucket. Which solution meets the requirement to provide proper permissions?
answer_text: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
explaination_text: Cognito Identity Pools map authenticated users to IAM roles. Those IAM roles must have the appropriate S3 permissions to access the data.

question_text: S3 standard assets accessed frequently for 30 days, then inconsistently. Optimize costs while maintaining HA and resiliency. Which combination of actions? (Choose two.)
answer_text: A. Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days. B. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.
explaination_text: Intelligent-Tiering is ideal for inconsistent access patterns after the initial 30 days. Cleaning up incomplete uploads removes 'hidden' storage costs from failed large uploads.

question_text: Website hosted on S3 with an EC2 API. Sudden increase in sales requests expected. Ensure all requests are processed successfully. What should be recommended?
answer_text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network traffic.
explaination_text: CloudFront offloads static content traffic from the origin. Auto Scaling ensures the EC2 API tier has enough compute power to handle surges in dynamic sales requests.

question_text: Run regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances and patch them on a schedule. Which solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
explaination_text: Amazon Inspector performs vulnerability scanning. Systems Manager Patch Manager automates the deployment of OS patches across the fleet.

question_text: A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances and must encrypt the data at rest. What should a solutions architect do?
answer_text: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
explaination_text: RDS supports encryption at rest using AWS KMS keys. This must be enabled at the time the DB instance is created.

question_text: Migrate 20 TB of data to AWS within 30 days. Network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps. What should a solutions architect do?
answer_text: Use AWS Snowball.
explaination_text: With 15 Mbps, 20 TB would take months to upload over the internet. AWS Snowball is a physical device used to transport massive datasets quickly and offline.

question_text: Provide employees secure access to confidential files. Windows server is running out of capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements?
answer_text: Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate with on-premises Active Directory. Configure AWS Client VPN.
explaination_text: FSx provides managed Windows storage with AD integration for permissions. Client VPN allows secure remote access for employees.

question_text: Application disruptions occur every month at midnight when CPU utilization peaks to 100% for financial calculations. Recommend how to avoid downtime?
answer_text: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
explaination_text: Scheduled scaling allows you to proactively launch extra instances before a known, predictable surge occurs, preventing CPU saturation.

question_text: Allow customers to use on-premises Active Directory to download S3 files via SFTP client with LEAST operational overhead and NO changes to customer apps.
answer_text: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
explaination_text: AWS Transfer Family allows for a fully managed SFTP service that bridges S3 and standard SFTP clients while supporting AD for identity management.

question_text: Provision large EC2 instances from an AMI with minimum initialization latency to meet sudden surges in demand. Which solution?
answer_text: Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
explaination_text: Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) ensures that EBS volumes created from snapshots have full performance instantly, skipping the lazy-loading phase.

question_text: Multi-tier web application uses Aurora MySQL. Credentials must be encrypted and rotated every 14 days with LEAST operational effort. What should be done?
answer_text: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.
explaination_text: AWS Secrets Manager natively supports automatic rotation of Aurora credentials and integrates with KMS for encryption.

question_text: RDS MySQL read replicas experience lag during peak loads. Reduce replication lag as much as possible with minimal changes to code and overhead. Which solution?
answer_text: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.
explaination_text: Aurora replicas share the same storage as the primary, resulting in near-zero replication lag compared to standard RDS MySQL binary log replication.

question_text: Create a DR plan for high-volume Aurora MySQL platform. Replicate data to secondary Region MOST cost-effectively. Which solution?
answer_text: Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.
explaination_text: Aurora Global Database provides low-latency regional replication. Using a single instance in the secondary region is more cost-effective than a multi-node cluster.

question_text: Custom application with embedded credentials retrieves RDS MySQL data. Make more secure with least amount of programming effort. What should be done?
answer_text: Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule.
explaination_text: Moving credentials to Secrets Manager removes hardcoded secrets. Secrets Manager can automate the rotation without requiring application changes beyond fetching the secret.

question_text: A website behind an ALB with an Aurora database is vulnerable to SQL injection. How should the company resolve this issue?
answer_text: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
